# Goal
Operator directives (2026-10-20, verbatim): "let's try to also implement using jj as git manager from now on on shokunin runs"; "make sure we are always swarming heavily though". This wave is the study-and-falsify wave for moving shokunin lane-repo VCS writes to Jujutsu (jj 0.45.1 at ~/.local/bin/jj) in colocated mode: git stays the backend and the GitHub remotes are unchanged. The orchestrator integrates; every seat advises.

# Planned integration (what you test or attack)
- Helper /home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin/scripts/hyaku/jj-lane.sh (written and selftested 16/16 in sandboxes; read it, never edit it): `init <lane-dir> <id>` colocates when no .jj exists and sets repo config user.name/user.email = lane identity, snapshot.auto-track = "none()", trunk() = "<branch>@origin", and tracks <branch>@origin. `commit <lane-dir> --as <id> -m <msg> -- <paths>` takes a flock, runs `jj file track` and then `jj commit` on ONLY those paths, moves the branch bookmark, and pushes; on a rejected push it fetches, rebases only the unpushed commits, and retries; it prints the pushed hash. `push` and `state` (read-only, via --ignore-working-copy) round it out.
- Observed so far (helper selftest, jj 0.45.1):
  - git HEAD stays attached right after init. It becomes detached after jj mutations and points at @- (the branch tip once the bookmark moves), so `@{u}` breaks while `git rev-parse <branch>` works.
  - jj resets the git index on every mutation, which destroys `git add`-staged entries.
  - `jj commit <paths>` keeps @'s author unless `jj metaedit --update-author` runs first.
  - `jj git push` can ship a commit with a conflicted tree. The helper refuses that case.
  - `jj config set` without --ignore-working-copy snapshots with the default auto-track and tracks every untracked file. Fixed in the helper's init.
- Lanes are colocated between rounds. L1s and closures commit lane-repo work through the helper. Fleet-root commits stay on scripts/hyaku/fleet-commit.sh (git + flock) unless evidence shows jj is safe there.
- These protocol invariants must survive:
  - landed = committed AND pushed before a report cites the hash;
  - a cited hash stays an ancestor of the branch (pushed commits are never amended or rewritten);
  - every lane commit carries the lane identity `<id>-shokunin <<id>@shokunin.local>`;
  - commits are pathspec-limited;
  - LOG.md is append-only;
  - .ufo/state/ is never committed.

# Hard safety rules (every seat)
- NEVER run any `jj` command whose working directory or -R/--repository is /home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin or anything under it. That covers the live fleet root and the live lane repos, and six lane rounds are running in them right now. Even `jj log` snapshots or imports state (the mado round-14 incident). jj runs ONLY in your sandbox /fast/scratch/jj-wave/<your seat name>/ (mkdir -p it). Run `jj help` from there too.
- Live repos are read-only for you:
  - allowed: cat, grep, find, and `git -C <live> log|show|ls-files|rev-parse|status|diff`;
  - allowed for copying out: `git clone`, `git clone --bare`, `cp -a` and `rsync -a`;
  - never write, commit, stage, stash, checkout or fetch in a live repo;
  - never execute fleet or lane scripts that could resolve to live paths. Replicate their commands by hand inside your sandbox.
- Never push to a real remote. In a sandbox, point `origin` at a sandbox bare repo and confirm it with `git remote -v` before any push or fetch.
- Write exactly one report file, at the `Report:` path given at the end of your item. That path is relative to /home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin, so write it at /home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin/<that path>. Your only other writes go inside your own sandbox. Remove the sandbox when done, unless it preserves a failure you cite; in that case name its path.
- Report shape: findings first (observed facts, each with the exact command and an output excerpt), then inference marked [INFERENCE], then recommendations. An unrun check has not passed.
- Operator tooling authorization (2026-10-19): you may install or upgrade tools that help the task. Read /home/vgpnk/.omp/agent/RULES.md first. All pacman transactions are paused host-wide, so use uv tool, npx or official binaries only, and record any install. Never restart a host service.

/skill:godspeed

# Target
Run an empirical jj-colocation trial of the FLEET ROOT repo (/home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin, branch master; the lane repos inside it are gitignored as `*-shokunin/`). Your sandbox is /fast/scratch/jj-wave/JjTrialFleetRoot/. This trial decides whether the fleet root may also move to jj.

# Change
1. **Build the sandbox.** Run `git clone --bare /home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin /fast/scratch/jj-wave/JjTrialFleetRoot/remote.git`, then `git clone /fast/scratch/jj-wave/JjTrialFleetRoot/remote.git /fast/scratch/jj-wave/JjTrialFleetRoot/fleet`. Overlay the live untracked and ignored content with `rsync -a --exclude=.git --exclude=.jj --exclude='*-shokunin/' --exclude=.tower/worktrees /home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin/ /fast/scratch/jj-wave/JjTrialFleetRoot/fleet/`. Never copy .tower/worktrees: their .git files point at the live repo.
2. **Colocate.** Run `jj git init --colocate` and set user.name protocol-shokunin, user.email protocol@shokunin.local and snapshot.auto-track "none()". Time `jj status`. Record git HEAD attachment and the `git status --porcelain` delta.
3. **Mixed writers.** Reproduce BY HAND (never execute scripts/hyaku/fleet-commit.sh or append-closure.py: both default to live paths) the git sequence fleet-commit.sh runs: `git add -- <report>`, then `git commit -m ... -- <report>`, then `git push origin HEAD:master`. Run it after jj colocation, and answer:
   - Does the git commit land on master or on a detached HEAD?
   - Does the next jj command import it cleanly?
   - Does the push carry it?
   Repeat the same pair with jj as the writer: `jj file track` + `jj commit <paths>` + bookmark move + `jj git push`.
4. **Concurrency.** Run two writers concurrently under one flock: a jj commit of file X and a git commit of file Y. Check for divergent changes, conflicted bookmarks and lost commits.

# Acceptance
The report contains:
- a PASS/FAIL table;
- the exact HEAD and index behavior observed;
- a recommendation, with evidence, for one of three options: keep fleet-root commits on git, convert them to jj, or colocate the fleet root with git-only writers.

Lane bounds: leaf member — no subagent dispatch except your single labrat.

Report: write your scoped findings to .ufo/waves/hyaku/jj-w1/reports/JjTrialFleetRoot.md

tasks.name: JjAuditAudio
tasks.task:
/skill:godspeed

# Target
Statically audit, read-only, every git invocation in lane `audio`'s executable tooling under /home/vgpnk/Projects/shokunin/audio-shokunin. In scope:
- tools/ and scripts/;
- the gates and selftests named in SKILL.md;
- verifiers/;
- any *.sh, *.py, *.mjs, *.js or Makefile at the repo root.

Skip .git, .jj, corpus prose and .ufo/waves outputs. The branch is `main`.

# Change
Find the git calls. Search for shell `git ` and for subprocess/execFile/spawn calls that run git. For each call site record file:line and the exact command, then classify it:
- **A** assumes an attached branch HEAD or an upstream: `symbolic-ref`, `@{u}`, `--abbrev-ref HEAD`, `branch --show-current`, or HEAD used as a branch name.
- **B** mutates history, index or working tree: add, commit, stash, checkout, reset, rebase, push, pull, merge, clean, tag.
- **C** reads index or staging state: `diff --cached`, `ls-files -s`, `update-index`.
- **D** read-only and based on the HEAD commit: log, show, `rev-parse HEAD`, `diff <rev>`, plain ls-files. These are safe.

Also list the git hooks in use (.git/hooks entries that are not samples, or core.hooksPath) and any .gitattributes filters or eol rules. jj bypasses both.

# Acceptance
The report contains:
- the classified table (file:line · command · class · risk under jj colocation, where HEAD may be detached and jj manages the index · a jj-safe replacement);
- counts per class;
- this lane's top three risks.

Read-only: write nothing except the report.

Lane bounds: leaf member — no subagent dispatch.

Report: write your scoped findings to .ufo/waves/hyaku/jj-w1/reports/JjAuditAudio.md
